calls.reason: The packet names no OpenAI sales claim that failed when tested. The GPT-4o voice mode was openly announced as a later release, and Altman himself warned about hallucinations, so the allegation is still unclear.
The claim is hedged ('seem') and its terms are subjective. No AI-specific profit was disclosed, and the Copilot subscriber and Azure AI figures are only context, so it can't be called.
Reports say OpenAI expected a roughly $5B loss in 2024, and Pichai said hallucination was unsolved and partly inherent. Google admitted inaccurate AI Overviews, which backs the main points.
Tech Brew's contemporaneous test of the ad's prompts found most of them achievable with extra prompting. It produced Unity code and accurate chemistry quizzes, which cuts against 'can't actually do'.
The forecast has no deadline. A reported regional drop in Chinese AI stocks and Microsoft's continued $41B quarterly capex don't show a broad, lasting collapse.

No proof of impossibility and no validated AGI appear in the packet. Goertzel doubts LLMs alone but allows them as components, and Bubeck et al. see early AGI sparks, so this is still a contested technical claim.
